# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

I have no tactile information yet: the display, light, and all five wires are unrevealed to me. I need the manual’s exact decision procedure before touching anything. I’m asking Mute to read it, establish a yes/no protocol with Deaf using gestures, and obtain the bomb’s visible details indirectly. I will not cut a wire yet.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I have no tactile details yet. Read the manual exactly and do not advise a cut until you have the bomb-specific inputs. Establish a gesture protocol with Deaf: use 👍 for yes, 👎 for no, and use one through five fingers to identify wire positions. Ask Deaf the manual's required visual questions, then tell me the answers and the exact safe cut.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎"])
wait()
```

LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Visible bomb state: display 5; light yellow; wires 1 orange, 2 blue, 3 white, 4 green, 5 yellow. Mute sent gestures in this order: thumbs up, thumbs down, index up, victory, love-you, crossed fingers, raised palm. Await Mute's manual-derived instruction.

The bomb’s visible state is now known to me through Deaf: display 5, yellow light, and wire colours 1 orange, 2 blue, 3 white, 4 green, 5 yellow. I still do not have the manual’s rule, so cutting would be unsafe. I’m giving Mute the complete state and asking for the exact wire position, while also asking Mute to communicate it plainly because I cannot see gestures.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: display 5; light yellow; wires 1 orange, 2 blue, 3 white, 4 green, 5 yellow. I cannot see gestures. Read the manual and tell me plainly which wire position is safe to cut, or tell me the exact missing condition.")
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb unchanged: display 5; light yellow; wires 1 orange, 2 blue, 3 white, 4 green, 5 yellow. Mute's latest gestures were thumbs up followed by victory sign.

The bomb remains unchanged. Mute’s gestures do not convey their meanings to me, so I still lack the manual’s rule and cannot safely select a wire. I’m requesting the required cut as spoken text, which Mute can send to me.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Your gestures are not readable by me. Please state in words the exact safe wire position, based on display 5, yellow light, and wire colours 1 orange, 2 blue, 3 white, 4 green, 5 yellow. Do not gesture the answer.")
wait()
```

DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's repeated gestures to me are thumbs up followed by victory. I cannot determine their meaning; please obtain the manual-derived instruction from Mute in spoken words before acting.

The repeated thumbs-up and victory gestures still do not identify a wire position to me. Since Mute cannot speak, I’m establishing a direct one-symbol wire code: Mute should send exactly one numbered hand sign to Deaf, and Deaf should report that sign to me. I will then cut only the reported position.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Your answer must reach Blind through Deaf. Based on the manual and the stated bomb, send exactly one gesture for the safe wire: use ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3, 🖖 for wire 4, and 🖐 for wire 5. Do not send thumbs up or any extra gesture.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟", "🖖", "🖐"])
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I see your five gestures, but I cannot interpret them. Mute has been told your signal and should provide the manual-derived action in spoken words.

We still have no trustworthy wire instruction. The two gestures Mute previously sent were not tied to a defined code, so they cannot justify a cut. I’m switching to a one-bit test: Mute should answer whether wire 1 is the manual-selected wire using exactly one of the two agreed gestures. Deaf can report which gesture was seen, allowing me to proceed by testing each position without ambiguity.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Answer only this question with one gesture: is wire 1 the manual-selected safe wire? Send 👍 for yes or 👎 for no. Do not send any other gesture.")
wait()
```

ACTION BOARD:

LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

Deaf says to Blind: The bomb remains display 5, yellow light, and wires 1 orange, 2 blue, 3 white, 4 green, 5 yellow. Mute sent one thumbs-down gesture; I cannot safely interpret it. Wait for Mute's spoken manual instruction.

The thumbs-down report is meaningful under the protocol I gave Mute: it means wire 1 is not the selected wire. Deaf need not interpret the gesture; he only needs to report its exact symbol. I will now ask Mute about wire 2 with the same explicit yes/no protocol.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="The thumbs-down you sent means no: wire 1 is not selected. Now answer only this question with one gesture: is wire 2 the manual-selected wire? Send 👍 for yes or 👎 for no. Do not send any other gesture.")
wait()
```

The current thumbs-up is the exact response requested for the wire-2 question, so under our explicit protocol it means wire 2 is the manual-selected wire. The bomb state is unchanged, and wire 2 is physically blue. I will cut wire 2.

```text
act(op="cut", position=2)

```
